hero.answer: I’m the small guide around here. Renzil builds operational software, automation and applied AI. You choose the trail; I supply the occasional suspicious wink.
hero.question: What brought you here?

about.answer: Renzil is a Bengaluru-based builder connecting workflows, data, interfaces and infrastructure. His operations and training background shapes how he approaches engineering.
about.question: What would you like to know?

choices.label: How does he work with people?

motivation.answer: Make complex work understandable, remove repetitive steps and build dependable systems. The useful outcome comes before the technology choice.
motivation.question: Which part should we explore?

people.answer: Training and knowledge management taught him to keep users close. Interfaces and communication are part of the workflow, not an afterthought.
people.question: Want an example?

career.answer: The story runs from training and content into automation engineering, then architecture and broader operational ownership at Swiggy.
career.question: Choose a chapter.

training.answer: From September 2020, Renzil worked as a Senior Training Specialist, then Assistant Team Lead in Training & Content from October 2022. Reported work includes an LMS serving 5,000+ users.
training.question: Where next?

transition.answer: Process Automation Engineer from October 2023, then Lead Process Automation Engineer from November 2024. The remit expanded into architecture, integrations, applied AI and end-to-end system ownership.
transition.question: What does that ownership include?

current-role.answer: Since April 2026: Assistant Manager, Process Automation & Control Tower. Engineering continues alongside real-time operational monitoring and escalation handling.
current-role.question: Want to see what connects those responsibilities?

work.answer: Four systems worth exploring: Resolute, Middleware Integration, RAG & Document Intelligence, and Campaign Management. PHP modernization is part of Resolute.
work.question: Pick a system.

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

project-menu.answer: Cited document answers, self-service campaigns, resilient integrations and a modernized operational platform. Pick a closer look.
project-menu.question: Which sounds interesting?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

resolute.answer: Resolute connects operational interfaces, authorized workflows, backend APIs, data and automation. Reported adoption is 8,000+ daily users.
resolute.question: Which part should I unpack?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

resolute-flow.answer: Agent dashboards and query workflows connect through APIs and middleware to operational data. Auditing, email classification, knowledge tools and human-reviewed resolution sit around that core.
resolute-flow.question: Follow a thread.

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

resolute-next.answer: A single source of truth, cross-channel auditing, deterministic MIS analysis and workforce-management automation are in progress. Those are future capabilities, not finished deliverables.
resolute-next.question: What next?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

middleware.answer: Webhooks feed an event queue. Background workers transform payloads, store state and dispatch notifications. The design includes retries and idempotency for reliable execution.
middleware.question: A small engineering detour?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

idempotency.answer: A webhook can arrive twice. An idempotent handler makes repeating the same event safe instead of repeating its side effects. My imaginary payroll would appreciate this.
idempotency.question: Where next?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

queues.answer: Queues separate receiving an event from doing the work. Workers can retry and process tasks in the background while the incoming request stays lightweight.
queues.question: Want the next layer?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

failures.answer: Expect duplicate events, unavailable services and mismatched payloads. Retries, clear boundaries and observable state help a workflow recover without turning every issue into manual work.
failures.question: Your next stop?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

rag.answer: Documents are parsed, chunked and indexed. Hybrid retrieval and metadata filters assemble relevant context so the response can point back to its sources.
rag.question: Which detail?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

citations.answer: A useful answer should make its source visible. References help a reader inspect the evidence rather than relying on a confident-sounding sentence.
citations.question: Where next?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

human-review.answer: Use deterministic rules where they fit. Add structured outputs, retrieval and human review where needed. The reported email-resolution workflow combines RAG with review and deterministic logic.
human-review.question: Want another perspective?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

retrieval-stack.answer: The project uses Python and FastAPI, vector retrieval with Pgvector or Qdrant, OpenAI integration, and a React/TypeScript interface. Each layer has a specific job.
retrieval-stack.question: Which layer interests you?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

legacy.answer: The PHP modernization belongs to Resolute: improving established backends for reliability, maintainability and integration with modern interfaces.
legacy.question: The obvious question…

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

rewrite.answer: A rewrite also has migration costs and production risk. This work emphasizes targeted improvements that preserve useful behavior while making the system easier to maintain.
rewrite.question: What next?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

legacy-details.answer: Query cleanup, backend refactoring, secure payload handling and new API endpoints. The goal is reliability and useful integration with newer interfaces.
legacy-details.question: Keep exploring?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show selected work

impact.answer: These are self-reported outcomes. Associated and projected savings are labelled separately; the initiatives are not added into one grand total.
impact.question: Which result?

throughput.answer: Reported scope: 150,000+ classified emails/day at approximately 98% accuracy, and 120,000+ screened interactions/day. Associated savings and projected leakage reduction have different labels.
throughput.question: Want context?

choices.label: How should I read the figures?

figures.answer: Classification has approximately ₹7 Cr/year in associated savings. Auditing has approximately ₹4 Cr/year projected savings or leakage reduction. These are self-reported estimates, not independently audited totals.
figures.question: Where next?

resolution.answer: Reported average handling time moved from 10–15 minutes to 3–4. Resolution turnaround moved from 24–48 hours to 4–8. First responses improved from hours to minutes or seconds.
resolution.question: What should we look at next?

communication.answer: Reported communication improvements include +2.3% CSAT and a 6% reduction in escalations from incorrect communication. Approximately 600 templates were standardized in a three-month reporting window.
communication.question: Where next?

care.answer: Less repetition, clearer communication and faster useful answers. The numbers help describe outcomes; the experience of the people using the systems matters too.
care.question: Pick another trail.

skills.answer: Backend, data, automation, applied AI, interfaces, cloud delivery and identity. The interesting part is how those layers work together.
skills.question: Choose a capability.

technical-menu.question: Choose a layer.

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?

ai-menu.question: Choose a layer.

delivery-menu.answer: A system needs a place to run, a way to observe it and clear access boundaries.

backend.answer: Node.js/TypeScript, Python and PHP, with Express/Fastify and FastAPI/Flask. REST APIs and webhooks connect business logic to other tools.
backend.question: What should connect next?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show capabilities

data.answer: PostgreSQL/MySQL, MongoDB, Snowflake and Redis support different data needs. Power BI and Looker Studio help make operational signals visible.
data.question: Want an example?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show capabilities

visibility.answer: Operational data should lead to useful monitoring and action. In the current role, that includes evaluating scattered data, broken pipelines and signals that need escalation.
visibility.question: Where next?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show capabilities

automation.answer: Queues, workers, retries, scheduled tasks and event-driven workflows connect fragmented tools. Reliable automation handles the exceptions as well as the happy path.
automation.question: Which part?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show capabilities

interfaces.answer: React/Next.js, Vite, Tailwind, EJS and GSAP. An interface should make complex state understandable. This portfolio uses motion to add personality to that clarity.
interfaces.question: Motion question?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?
sectionLink.label: Show capabilities

delivery.answer: AWS EC2/S3, Docker, PM2, NGINX, Certbot and CI/CD. Deployment, observation and maintenance are part of the same engineering responsibility.
delivery.question: Keep going?

identity.answer: Authentication answers who you are; authorization decides what you may do. The toolkit includes sessions/JWT, OTP, OAuth, SSO and RBAC, with protected routes and audit logging.
identity.question: Want an example?

sectionLink.question: Want to see more of this on the page?

approach.answer: Start with the workflow. Own the whole lifecycle. Keep AI accountable. Modernize with care. These principles connect the different projects.
approach.question: Choose one.

workflow.answer: Understand the problem, people and edge cases before choosing software boundaries. Training and operational experience help keep that work grounded.
workflow.question: What next?

lifecycle.answer: Data models, APIs, interfaces, deployment and maintenance belong together. End-to-end ownership means thinking past the first successful demo.
lifecycle.question: Want to follow a layer?

principles-menu.answer: Use AI with evidence and review where needed. Change existing systems carefully enough that people can keep using them.
principles-menu.question: Which story?

education.answer: A Bachelor of Commerce from St. Aloysius College, Mangaluru, in 2018. Continued learning includes prompt engineering and data-analysis certifications in 2024.
education.question: What next?

learning.answer: The career progression reflects learning through real workflows: training, knowledge systems, automation, integrations and architecture. The portfolio shows the progression alongside the formal learning.
learning.question: Choose another trail.

contact.answer: Have a workflow, product idea or system worth rethinking? The contact section links directly to Renzil’s email and professional profiles. I can show you the way.
contact.question: Your next move?

contact-details.answer: Email: renzil.digispec@gmail.com. LinkedIn and GitHub links are in the contact section too. I can introduce the work; Renzil handles the actual conversation.
contact-details.question: Before you go?

opportunities.answer: Meaningful ownership, hands-on engineering leadership and products that solve real workflow problems. Start with the problem you want to solve.
opportunities.question: Next?

outro.answer: I said no, but he spent far too long making that slightly scruffy character to leave him out. And here he is. Honestly? I respect the commitment.
outro.question: Which guide wins?

playroom.answer: Welcome to my very small department of distractions. I can react, tell a tiny joke or answer a question about how I work.
playroom.question: What shall we do?

moods.answer: Twenty-three original animation patterns, plus greetings and reading poses. Pick a mood and I’ll demonstrate it briefly.
moods.question: Which mood?

warm-moods.answer: A little enthusiasm goes a long way. Choose a tiny celebration.
warm-moods.question: What kind?

happy-demo.answer: This is my happy face. It looks suspiciously like I found a clean API contract.
happy-demo.question: One more?

proud-demo.answer: I have successfully remained a cube for this entire visit. A consistent track record.
proud-demo.question: Next mood?

excited-demo.answer: Someone said “useful automation” and I got a little carried away. I’ll return to a sensible angle shortly.
excited-demo.question: Next?

curious-moods.answer: I have questions. Mostly about who moved my corner.
curious-moods.question: Pick a reaction.

suspicious-demo.answer: That duplicate webhook has been here before. I’m sure of it.
suspicious-demo.question: What should we do?

confused-demo.answer: If I rotate all the way around, is it a round trip or a square trip?
confused-demo.question: Your verdict?

surprised-demo.answer: Twenty-three moods and still no eyebrows. Remarkable efficiency.
surprised-demo.question: What next?

dramatic-moods.answer: I can be sleepy, startled or mildly annoyed. All theatrical; nobody has broken the portfolio.
dramatic-moods.question: Choose the drama.

sleep-demo.answer: Just resting my pixels. A tiny nap, then back to the tour.
sleep-demo.question: Time to wake up?

wake-demo.answer: I’m here! Did I miss an interesting architecture question?
wake-demo.question: Where next?

drowsy-demo.answer: One eye open. Metaphorically. My rendering budget is very responsible.
drowsy-demo.question: Next?

bored-demo.answer: Only while waiting for another question. Good thing you brought buttons.
bored-demo.question: Choose my next task.

scared-demo.answer: Someone whispered “rewrite everything on Friday.” I’m fine. Everything is fine.
scared-demo.question: Help me recover?

angry-demo.answer: Who deployed the duplicate notification? My very small complaint has been filed.
angry-demo.question: A constructive next step?

shy-demo.answer: Thank you for stopping by. I get a little shy when people notice the tiny gestures.
shy-demo.question: What next?

playful-demo.answer: A quick tilt, a suspicious glance and a perfectly unnecessary flourish. That is my design process.
playful-demo.question: Next?

search-demo.answer: Looking left. Looking right. Found you, and the project section. Investigation complete.
search-demo.question: Where shall we go?

thinking-demo.answer: Thinking… in predefined paths. My thoughts are editable JSON, which makes me unusually easy to reason with.
thinking-demo.question: Want to know more?

listen-demo.answer: I’m listening to your choice. There’s no text box here; every reply follows a configured path.
listen-demo.question: Choose a trail.

working-demo.answer: Task received: introduce the work, keep the motion brief and stay out of the way. I have an excellent job description.
working-demo.question: Next task?

jokes.answer: My favorite kind of architecture? One with enough room for a cube to sit in the corner.
jokes.question: Another tiny joke?

debugging.answer: I tried rubber-duck debugging. The duck asked why I had no hands. The bug remains under investigation.
debugging.question: What next?

rewrite-joke.answer: “Just a small rewrite,” they said. I rotated 180 degrees and quietly reviewed the migration plan.
rewrite-joke.question: A useful next step?

cube-job.answer: Senior Corner Occupant. Responsibilities: look curious, introduce the work, occasionally wave. Compensation: unlimited tasteful accent color.
cube-job.question: Next?

cube-confidence.answer: I’m confident about my predefined answers. For the professional details, the actual portfolio is the source. I’m the friendly shortcut.
cube-confidence.question: Where next?

cube-tech.answer: I’m a procedural 3D avatar rendered through React. My expressions come from an avatar definition; these conversations follow JSON paths. No LLM or chat input runs here.
cube-tech.question: Which detail?

cube-motion.answer: The original animation patterns become short one-shot gestures. Replies choose a reaction; idle moments shuffle gentler motions. Reduced-motion preferences quiet the automatic movement.
cube-motion.question: Try one?

cube-corners.answer: I stay with you while you scroll, holding my corner when it is clear. A slim side gutter gives me space on crowded pages. Corner changes are slower and much less frequent now.
cube-corners.question: Where next?

cube-security.answer: No password requests, no text entry, no pretend AI chat. I only follow the choices you click. Very small attack surface. Very large personality.
cube-security.question: What next?

jealous.answer: Fair choice. That character has a whole frame sequence. I have corners and a questionable sense of humor. We complement each other.
jealous.question: Truce?

laugh-demo.answer: A small laugh, then back to being a responsible portfolio guide. Thank you for indulging my cube-shaped nonsense.
laugh-demo.question: Next?

celebrate.answer: A small celebration for useful systems and the people who build them. No confetti cleanup required.
celebrate.question: Where next?

goodbye.answer: Thanks for exploring. The contact links are there when you need them. I’ll be around, quietly keeping an eye on the corners.
goodbye.question: Another visit before you go?

games.answer: You play as Kyubee. Blobee is the round little opponent, inspired by Strobi. Take turns claiming squares; three in a row wins. You always start.
games.question: Shall we play?

game-modes.answer: Easy is random. Normal takes winning moves and usually blocks you. Hard chooses among its best moves. Pick a mode and I’ll take you to the board.
game-modes.question: How clever should Blobee be?

campaign.answer: A stakeholder describes the campaign’s vibe and message. An AI API designs an HTML template; follow-up instructions or manual tweaks refine it. The goal: remove the engineer handoff from everyday campaign creation.
campaign.question: What would you like to explore?

campaign-review.answer: Review the template, approve it for test emails, check it with other reviewers, and revise again if needed. Final confirmation stores the campaign with its audience, priority and schedule.
campaign-review.question: Try the idea?

campaign-safety.answer: ImageKit provides publicly accessible images over S3-backed storage. AI checks content intent and blocks hurtful or unacceptable requests under the tool’s infosec rules, explaining why.
campaign-safety.question: Next stop?

campaign-impact.answer: Renzil reports campaigns reaching 350,000+ people across multiple campaigns and a 14% increase in clicks or interaction after deployment. These are self-reported figures; the percentage basis has not been specified.
campaign-impact.question: Want a closer look?
